facts.statement: Bromsgroveia was a predatory archosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic in England.
facts.quote: Bromsgroveia is an extinct genus of predatory ctenosauriscid archosaur from the Middle Triassic Bromsgrove Sandstone of England.

facts.statement: The holotype of Bromsgroveia is a right ilium collected from Coton Green Quarry in Warwickshire.
facts.quote: The holotype is a right ilium (WM G3a, b; cast as NHMUK PV R 2549) and it was collected from Coton Green Quarry, Warwickshire where the Bromsgrove Sandstone can be found.

facts.statement: In 1842, Owen incorrectly assigned the holotype of Bromsgroveia to Labyrinthodon pachygnathus, believing it to be a large frog.
facts.quote: Owen (1842) assigned WM G3a alongside remains now known to belong to the Mastodonsauridae to Labyrinthodon pachygnathus (now Mastodonsaurus); Owen believed it was a large frog.

facts.statement: Galton named and described the species Bromsgroveia walkeri in 1985, classifying it within the Rauisuchia.
facts.quote: Galton (1985) named and described Bromsgroveia walkeri based on WM G3a as the holotype, and he also classified it into Rauisuchia.

facts.statement: Additional remains including vertebrae and teeth found in the 1980s and 1990s were described by Galton and Walker in 1996.
facts.quote: Further remains found during the 1980s and 1990s included mid-cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, an ischium, and isolated teeth collected from the Bromsgrove Sandstone at Warwick, Leamington Spa, and Bromsgrove; they were described in a revision of the Bromsgroveia genus by Galton & Walker (1996).

facts.statement: Bromsgroveia is closely related to Ctenosauriscus and belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae.
facts.quote: Bromsgroveia was closely related to Ctenosauriscus, and together with a few other genera they make up Ctenosauriscidae.

facts.statement: The pelvic girdle of Bromsgroveia links it to Ctenosauriscus, Lotosaurus, Arizonasaurus, and Hypselorhachis.
facts.quote: The pelvic girdle in Bromsgroveia unites this taxon with Ctenosauriscus, Lotosaurus, Arizonasaurus, and Hypselorhachis.

facts.statement: The parent group of Bromsgroveia is the family Ctenosauriscidae.
Bromsgroveia is classified within the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: Ctenosauriscids, the family to which Bromsgroveia belongs, were rauisuchians related to the ancestors of modern crocodiles and alligators.
rejected.quote: Ctenosauriscids were a group of rauisuchians that was related to the ancestors of modern crocodiles and alligators.
